properties.text: Federated learning for speech keeps data decentralized on client devices, enabling collaborative model training while mitigating the privacy risks associated with centralized data storage.

support.paper: sotto voce federated speech recognition with differential privacy guarantees
support.quote: In this paper, we offer a potential solution for learning an ML model across multiple organizations where we can provide mathematical guarantees limiting privacy loss. We use a Federated Learning approach built on a strong foundation of Differential Privacy techniques.

support.paper: privacy preserving speech based depression diagnosis via federated learning
support.quote: in this paper, we demonstrate for the first time that speech-based depression diagnosis models can be trained in a privacy-preserving way using federated learning, which enables collaborative model training while keeping the private speech data decentralized on clients' devices.

support.paper: privacy preserving speech based depression diagnosis via federated learning
support.quote: However, this centralized training requiring data to be stored at a server raises the risks of severe voice data breaches, and people may not be willing to share their speech data with third parties due to privacy concerns.

support.paper: user level differential privacy against attribute inference attack of speech emotion recognition in federated learning
support.quote: While FL provides good intuition to safeguard privacy by keeping the data on local devices, prior work has shown that privacy attacks, such as attribute inference attacks, are achievable for SER systems trained using FL.

support.paper: robust federated learning against adversarial attacks for speech emotion recognition
support.quote: However, the speech data cannot be protected when it is uploaded and processed on servers in the internet-of-things applications of speech emotion recognition.

support.paper: federated learning in asr not as easy as you think
support.quote: Federated learning is a decentralized optimization strategy that has been proposed to address such concerns. Utilizing this approach, private data is used for on-device training.

support.paper: federated acoustic modeling for automatic speech recognition
support.quote: In this paper, we investigate federated acoustic modeling using data from multiple clients. A client’s data is stored on a local data server and the clients communicate only model parameters with a central server, and not their data.

properties.text: The family encompasses methods for various speech tasks, including automatic speech recognition (ASR), keyword spotting (KWS), and speech emotion recognition (SER).

fairness in criminal justice risk assess.quote: We draw on the existing literatures in criminology, computer science, and statistics to provide an integrated examination of fairness and accuracy in criminal justice risk assessments.

fairness in criminal justice risk assess.subject: Empirical illustration using arraignments data
fairness in criminal justice risk assess.claim: The authors provide an empirical illustration using data from arraignments.
fairness in criminal justice risk assess.quote: We also provide an empirical illustration using data from arraignments.

counterfactual fairness.subject: counterfactual fairness
counterfactual fairness.claim: The paper develops a framework for modeling fairness using tools from causal inference.
counterfactual fairness.quote: In this paper, we develop a framework for modeling fairness using tools from causal inference.

counterfactual fairness.subject: counterfactual fairness
counterfactual fairness.claim: A decision is fair towards an individual if it is the same in the actual world and a counterfactual world where the individual belonged to a different demographic group.
counterfactual fairness.quote: Our definition of counterfactual fairness captures the intuition that a decision is fair towards an individual if it the same in (a) the actual world and (b) a counterfactual world where the individual belonged to a different demographic group.

counterfactual fairness.subject: counterfactual fairness
counterfactual fairness.claim: The framework is demonstrated on a real-world problem of fair prediction of success in law school.
counterfactual fairness.quote: We demonstrate our framework on a real-world problem of fair prediction of success in law school.

generative poisoning attack method again.subject: direct gradient method
generative poisoning attack method again.claim: The direct gradient method applies a traditional gradient-based approach to generate poisoned data against neural networks by leveraging the gradient of the target model with respect to normal data.
generative poisoning attack method again.quote: In this work, we first examine the possibility of applying traditional gradient-based method (named as the direct gradient method) to generate poisoned data against NNs by leveraging the gradient of the target model w.r.t. the normal data.

generative poisoning attack method again.subject: generative method
generative poisoning attack method again.claim: The proposed generative method uses an auto-encoder generator updated by a reward function of the loss to accelerate the generation rate of poisoned data.
generative poisoning attack method again.quote: We then propose a generative method to accelerate the generation rate of the poisoned data: an auto-encoder (generator) used to generate poisoned data is updated by a reward function of the loss, and the target NN model (discriminator) receives the poisoned data to calculate the loss w.r.t. the normal data.

generative poisoning attack method again.subject: generative method
generative poisoning attack method again.claim: The generative method can speed up the poisoned data generation rate by up to 239.38x compared with the direct gradient method, with slightly lower model accuracy degradation.
generative poisoning attack method again.quote: Our experiment results show that the generative method can speed up the poisoned data generation rate by up to 239.38x compared with the direct gradient method, with slightly lower model accuracy degradation.

generative poisoning attack method again.subject: countermeasure
generative poisoning attack method again.claim: A countermeasure is designed to detect poisoning attack methods by checking the loss of the target model.
generative poisoning attack method again.quote: A countermeasure is also designed to detect such poisoning attack methods by checking the loss of the target model.

generative poisoning attack method again.subject: poisoning attack
generative poisoning attack method again.claim: There is still very limited knowledge about how poisoning attacks can be implemented on neural networks, especially deep neural networks.
generative poisoning attack method again.quote: Although poisoning attack against support vector machines (SVM) has been extensively studied before, there is still very limited knowledge about how such attack can be implemented on neural networks (NN), especially DNNs.

membership inference attacks against mac.subject: membership inference attack
membership inference attacks against mac.claim: The paper focuses on the basic membership inference attack, which determines if a data record was in the model's training dataset given black-box access to the model.
membership inference attacks against mac.quote: We focus on the basic membership inference attack: given a data record and black-box access to a model, determine if the record was in the model's training dataset.

membership inference attacks against mac.subject: inference model
membership inference attacks against mac.claim: The authors train their own inference model to recognize differences in the target model's predictions on inputs it trained on versus inputs it did not train on.
membership inference attacks against mac.quote: To perform membership inference against a target model, we make adversarial use of machine learning and train our own inference model to recognize differences in the target model's predictions on the inputs that it trained on versus the inputs that it did not train on.

membership inference attacks against mac.subject: commercial machine learning models
membership inference attacks against mac.claim: Classification models trained by commercial providers such as Google and Amazon can be vulnerable to membership inference attacks.
membership inference attacks against mac.quote: Using realistic datasets and classification tasks, including a hospital discharge dataset whose membership is sensitive from the privacy perspective, we show that these models can be vulnerable to membership inference attacks.

membership inference attacks against mac.subject: hospital discharge dataset
membership inference attacks against mac.claim: The study uses a hospital discharge dataset, whose membership is sensitive from a privacy perspective, to evaluate the vulnerability of models to membership inference attacks.
membership inference attacks against mac.quote: Using realistic datasets and classification tasks, including a hospital discharge dataset whose membership is sensitive from the privacy perspective, we show that these models can be vulnerable to membership inference attacks.

equality of opportunity in supervised le.subject: criterion for discrimination against a specified sensitive attribute
equality of opportunity in supervised le.claim: The paper proposes a criterion for discrimination against a specified sensitive attribute in supervised learning.
equality of opportunity in supervised le.quote: We propose a criterion for discrimination against a specified sensitive attribute in supervised learning, where the goal is to predict some target based on available features.

equality of opportunity in supervised le.subject: optimal adjustment of learned predictors
equality of opportunity in supervised le.claim: The authors show how to optimally adjust any learned predictor to remove discrimination according to their definition.
equality of opportunity in supervised le.quote: Assuming data about the predictor, target, and membership in the protected group are available, we show how to optimally adjust any learned predictor so as to remove discrimination according to our definition.

equality of opportunity in supervised le.subject: framework for discrimination removal
equality of opportunity in supervised le.claim: The framework improves incentives by shifting the cost of poor classification from disadvantaged groups to the decision maker.
equality of opportunity in supervised le.quote: Our framework also improves incentives by shifting the cost of poor classification from disadvantaged groups to the decision maker, who can respond by improving the classification accuracy.

mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.subject: pipeline
mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.claim: The pipeline automatically downloads and aligns spoken Wikipedia data to generate corpora for many languages.
mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.quote: Our pipeline automatically downloads and aligns this data.

mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.subject: German corpus
mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.claim: The resulting German corpus totals 293h of audio, with 71h aligned in full sentences and 86h of sentences with some missing words.
mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.quote: The resulting German corpus currently totals 293h of audio, of which we align 71h in full sentences and another 86h of sentences with some missing words.

mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.subject: English corpus
mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.claim: The English corpus consists of 287h, with 27h aligned in full sentence and 157h with some missing words.
mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.quote: The English corpus consists of 287h, for which we align 27h in full sentence and 157h with some missing words.

mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.subject: corpus alignment
mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.claim: A significant portion of the aligned data consists of sentences with some missing words rather than full sentences.
mining the spoken wikipedia for speech d.quote: of which we align 71h in full sentences and another 86h of sentences with some missing words.

communication efficient learning of deep.subject: Federated Learning
communication efficient learning of deep.claim: Federated Learning is a decentralized approach that leaves training data distributed on mobile devices and learns a shared model by aggregating locally-computed updates.
communication efficient learning of deep.quote: We advocate an alternative that leaves the training data distributed on the mobile devices, and learns a shared model by aggregating locally-computed updates. We term this decentralized approach Federated Learning.

communication efficient learning of deep.subject: iterative model averaging
communication efficient learning of deep.claim: The paper presents a practical method for the federated learning of deep networks based on iterative model averaging.
communication efficient learning of deep.quote: We present a practical method for the federated learning of deep networks based on iterative model averaging, and conduct an extensive empirical evaluation, considering five different model architectures and four datasets.

communication efficient learning of deep.subject: Federated Learning
communication efficient learning of deep.claim: The approach is robust to the unbalanced and non-IID data distributions that are a defining characteristic of this setting.
communication efficient learning of deep.quote: These experiments demonstrate the approach is robust to the unbalanced and non-IID data distributions that are a defining characteristic of this setting.

communication efficient learning of deep.subject: Federated Learning
communication efficient learning of deep.claim: The method achieves a reduction in required communication rounds by 10-100x as compared to synchronized stochastic gradient descent.
communication efficient learning of deep.quote: Communication costs are the principal constraint, and we show a reduction in required communication rounds by 10-100x as compared to synchronized stochastic gradient descent.

deep residual learning for image recogni.subject: residual learning framework
deep residual learning for image recogni.claim: The paper presents a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously.
deep residual learning for image recogni.quote: We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously.

deep residual learning for image recogni.subject: residual networks
deep residual learning for image recogni.claim: Residual networks explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions.
deep residual learning for image recogni.quote: We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions.

deep residual learning for image recogni.subject: residual networks
deep residual learning for image recogni.claim: Residual networks are easier to optimize and can gain accuracy from considerably increased depth.
deep residual learning for image recogni.quote: We provide comprehensive empirical evidence showing that these residual networks are easier to optimize, and can gain accuracy from considerably increased depth.

deep residual learning for image recogni.subject: residual nets
deep residual learning for image recogni.claim: An ensemble of residual nets with a depth of up to 152 layers achieves 3.57% error on the ImageNet test set.
deep residual learning for image recogni.quote: An ensemble of these residual nets achieves 3.57% error on the ImageNet test set.

deep residual learning for image recogni.subject: residual nets
deep residual learning for image recogni.claim: The result of the residual nets won the 1st place on the ILSVRC 2015 classification task.
deep residual learning for image recogni.quote: This result won the 1st place on the ILSVRC 2015 classification task.

deep residual learning for image recogni.subject: deep residual nets
deep residual learning for image recogni.claim: Solely due to extremely deep representations, a 28% relative improvement is obtained on the COCO object detection dataset.
deep residual learning for image recogni.quote: Solely due to our extremely deep representations, we obtain a 28% relative improvement on the COCO object detection dataset.

deepfool a simple and accurate method to.subject: DeepFool
deepfool a simple and accurate method to.claim: The paper proposes the DeepFool algorithm to efficiently compute perturbations that fool deep networks and reliably quantify the robustness of these classifiers.
deepfool a simple and accurate method to.quote: In this paper, we fill this gap and propose the DeepFool algorithm to efficiently compute perturbations that fool deep networks, and thus reliably quantify the robustness of these classifiers.

deepfool a simple and accurate method to.subject: DeepFool
deepfool a simple and accurate method to.claim: Extensive experimental results show that the DeepFool approach outperforms recent methods in the task of computing adversarial perturbations and making classifiers more robust.
deepfool a simple and accurate method to.quote: Extensive experimental results show that our approach outperforms recent methods in the task of computing adversarial perturbations and making classifiers more robust.

deepfool a simple and accurate method to.subject: state-of-the-art deep classifiers
deepfool a simple and accurate method to.claim: Prior to this work, no effective methods had been proposed to accurately compute the robustness of state-of-the-art deep classifiers to small perturbations on large-scale datasets.
deepfool a simple and accurate method to.quote: Despite the importance of this phenomenon, no effective methods have been proposed to accurately compute the robustness of state-of-the-art deep classifiers to such perturbations on large-scale datasets.

librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.subject: LibriSpeech
librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.claim: The paper introduces a new corpus of read English speech suitable for training and evaluating speech recognition systems.
librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.quote: This paper introduces a new corpus of read English speech, suitable for training and evaluating speech recognition systems.

librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.subject: LibriSpeech
librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.claim: The corpus is derived from audiobooks that are part of the LibriVox project and contains 1000 hours of speech sampled at 16 kHz.
librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.quote: The LibriSpeech corpus is derived from audiobooks that are part of the LibriVox project, and contains 1000 hours of speech sampled at 16 kHz.

librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.subject: LibriSpeech
librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.claim: Acoustic models trained on LibriSpeech give lower error rate on the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) test sets than models trained on WSJ itself.
librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.quote: We show that acoustic models trained on LibriSpeech give lower error rate on the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) test sets than models trained on WSJ itself.

librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.subject: Kaldi scripts
librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.claim: The authors are releasing Kaldi scripts that make it easy to build these systems.
librispeech an asr corpus based on publi.quote: We are also releasing Kaldi scripts that make it easy to build these systems.

using machine teaching to identify optim.subject: bilevel optimization formulation
using machine teaching to identify optim.claim: Optimal training-set attack can be formulated as a bilevel optimization problem.
using machine teaching to identify optim.quote: First we show that optimal training-set attack can be formulated as a bilevel optimization problem.

using machine teaching to identify optim.subject: gradient methods on an implicit function
using machine teaching to identify optim.claim: For machine learners with certain Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, the bilevel problem can be solved efficiently using gradient methods on an implicit function.
using machine teaching to identify optim.quote: Then we show that for machine learners with certain Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions we can solve the bilevel problem efficiently using gradient methods on an implicit function.

using machine teaching to identify optim.subject: optimal training-set attacks
using machine teaching to identify optim.claim: The paper demonstrates optimal training-set attacks on Support Vector Machines, logistic regression, and linear regression with extensive experiments.
using machine teaching to identify optim.quote: As examples, we demonstrate optimal training-set attacks on Support VectorMachines, logistic regression, and linear regression with extensive experiments.

using machine teaching to identify optim.subject: training-set attacks
using machine teaching to identify optim.claim: Understanding training-set attacks is important as more intelligent agents equipped with learning capability can potentially be hacked via data they receive from the environment.
using machine teaching to identify optim.quote: Understanding training-set attacks is important as more intelligent agents (e.g. spam filters and robots) are equipped with learning capability and can potentially be hacked via data they receive from the environment.

explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.subject: neural networks
explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.claim: The primary cause of neural networks' vulnerability to adversarial perturbation is their linear nature.
explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.quote: We argue instead that the primary cause of neural networks' vulnerability to adversarial perturbation is their linear nature.

explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.subject: adversarial examples
explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.claim: Adversarial examples generalize across architectures and training sets.
explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.quote: This explanation is supported by new quantitative results while giving the first explanation of the most intriguing fact about them: their generalization across architectures and training sets.

explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.subject: adversarial example generation method
explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.claim: The linear nature view yields a simple and fast method of generating adversarial examples.
explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.quote: Moreover, this view yields a simple and fast method of generating adversarial examples.

explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.subject: adversarial training
explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.claim: Using the generated adversarial examples for adversarial training reduces the test set error of a maxout network on the MNIST dataset.
explaining and harnessing adversarial ex.quote: Using this approach to provide examples for adversarial training, we reduce the test set error of a maxout network on the MNIST dataset.

deep speech scaling up end to end speech.subject: Deep Speech
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.claim: Deep Speech is a state-of-the-art speech recognition system developed using end-to-end deep learning.
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.quote: We present a state-of-the-art speech recognition system developed using end-to-end deep learning.

deep speech scaling up end to end speech.subject: Deep Speech
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.claim: The system does not need hand-designed components to model background noise, reverberation, or speaker variation, but instead directly learns a function that is robust to such effects.
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.quote: In contrast, our system does not need hand-designed components to model background noise, reverberation, or speaker variation, but instead directly learns a function that is robust to such effects.

deep speech scaling up end to end speech.subject: RNN training system
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.claim: Key to the approach is a well-optimized RNN training system that uses multiple GPUs.
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.quote: Key to our approach is a well-optimized RNN training system that uses multiple GPUs, as well as a set of novel data synthesis techniques that allow us to efficiently obtain a large amount of varied data for training.

deep speech scaling up end to end speech.subject: data synthesis techniques
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.claim: A set of novel data synthesis techniques allows for the efficient obtaining of a large amount of varied data for training.
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.quote: Key to our approach is a well-optimized RNN training system that uses multiple GPUs, as well as a set of novel data synthesis techniques that allow us to efficiently obtain a large amount of varied data for training.

deep speech scaling up end to end speech.subject: Deep Speech
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.claim: Deep Speech outperforms previously published results on the Switchboard Hub5'00 dataset, achieving 16.0% error on the full test set.
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.quote: Our system, called Deep Speech, outperforms previously published results on the widely studied Switchboard Hub5'00, achieving 16.0% error on the full test set.

deep speech scaling up end to end speech.subject: Deep Speech
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.claim: Deep Speech handles challenging noisy environments better than widely used, state-of-the-art commercial speech systems.
deep speech scaling up end to end speech.quote: Deep Speech also handles challenging noisy environments better than widely used, state-of-the-art commercial speech systems.

intriguing properties of neural networks.subject: Deep neural networks
intriguing properties of neural networks.claim: There is no distinction between individual high level units and random linear combinations of high level units according to various methods of unit analysis.
intriguing properties of neural networks.quote: First, we find that there is no distinction between individual high level units and random linear combinations of high level units, according to various methods of unit analysis.

intriguing properties of neural networks.subject: Deep neural networks
intriguing properties of neural networks.claim: It suggests that it is the space, rather than the individual units, that contains of the semantic information in the high layers of neural networks.
intriguing properties of neural networks.quote: It suggests that it is the space, rather than the individual units, that contains of the semantic information in the high layers of neural networks.

intriguing properties of neural networks.subject: Deep neural networks
intriguing properties of neural networks.claim: Deep neural networks learn input-output mappings that are fairly discontinuous to a significant extend.
intriguing properties of neural networks.quote: Second, we find that deep neural networks learn input-output mappings that are fairly discontinuous to a significant extend.

intriguing properties of neural networks.subject: Imperceptible perturbation maximization
intriguing properties of neural networks.claim: The network can be caused to misclassify an image by applying a certain imperceptible perturbation, which is found by maximizing the network's prediction error.
intriguing properties of neural networks.quote: We can cause the network to misclassify an image by applying a certain imperceptible perturbation, which is found by maximizing the network's prediction error.

intriguing properties of neural networks.subject: Imperceptible perturbation maximization
intriguing properties of neural networks.claim: The same perturbation can cause a different network, that was trained on a different subset of the dataset, to misclassify the same input.
intriguing properties of neural networks.quote: In addition, the specific nature of these perturbations is not a random artifact of learning: the same perturbation can cause a different network, that was trained on a different subset of the dataset, to misclassify the same input.

evasion attacks against machine learning.subject: gradient-based approach
evasion attacks against machine learning.claim: The paper presents a simple but effective gradient-based approach to systematically assess the security of classification algorithms against evasion attacks.
evasion attacks against machine learning.quote: In this work, we present a simple but effective gradient-based approach that can be exploited to systematically assess the security of several, widely-used classification algorithms against evasion attacks.

evasion attacks against machine learning.subject: security evaluation framework
evasion attacks against machine learning.claim: The authors simulate attack scenarios with varying risk levels by increasing the attacker's knowledge and manipulation ability, following a recently proposed framework for security evaluation.
evasion attacks against machine learning.quote: Following a recently proposed framework for security evaluation, we simulate attack scenarios that exhibit different risk levels for the classifier by increasing the attacker's knowledge of the system and her ability to manipulate attack samples.

evasion attacks against machine learning.subject: PDF malware detection systems
evasion attacks against machine learning.claim: Systems for malware detection in PDF files can be easily evaded by the proposed attack approach.
evasion attacks against machine learning.quote: We evaluate our approach on the relevant security task of malware detection in PDF files, and show that such systems can be easily evaded.

evasion attacks against machine learning.subject: classifier designers
evasion attacks against machine learning.claim: The proposed evaluation method allows classifier designers to perform more informed model selection or parameter setting by providing a better picture of performance under evasion attacks.
evasion attacks against machine learning.quote: This gives the classifier designer a better picture of the classifier performance under evasion attacks, and allows him to perform a more informed model selection (or parameter setting).

poisoning attacks against support vector.subject: Poisoning Attacks against Support Vector Machines
poisoning attacks against support vector.claim: The proposed attack uses a gradient ascent strategy in which the gradient is computed based on properties of the SVM's optimal solution.
poisoning attacks against support vector.quote: The proposed attack uses a gradient ascent strategy in which the gradient is computed based on properties of the SVM's optimal solution.

poisoning attacks against support vector.subject: Poisoning Attacks against Support Vector Machines
poisoning attacks against support vector.claim: The method can be kernelized and enables the attack to be constructed in the input space even for non-linear kernels.
poisoning attacks against support vector.quote: This method can be kernelized and enables the attack to be constructed in the input space even for non-linear kernels.

poisoning attacks against support vector.subject: Poisoning Attacks against Support Vector Machines
poisoning attacks against support vector.claim: The gradient ascent procedure reliably identifies good local maxima of the non-convex validation error surface, which significantly increases the classifier's test error.
poisoning attacks against support vector.quote: We experimentally demonstrate that our gradient ascent procedure reliably identifies good local maxima of the non-convex validation error surface, which significantly increases the classifier's test error.

poisoning attacks against support vector.subject: Support Vector Machines
poisoning attacks against support vector.claim: Most learning algorithms assume that their training data comes from a natural or well-behaved distribution, an assumption that does not generally hold in security-sensitive settings.
poisoning attacks against support vector.quote: Central to the motivation for these attacks is the fact that most learning algorithms assume that their training data comes from a natural or well-behaved distribution. However, this assumption does not generally hold in security-sensitive settings.

ted lium an automatic speech recognition.subject: TED-LIUM
ted lium an automatic speech recognition.claim: The corpus was built during the IWSLT 2011 Evaluation Campaign and is composed of 118 hours of speech with its accompanying automatically aligned transcripts.
ted lium an automatic speech recognition.quote: This corpus was built during the IWSLT 2011 Evaluation Campaign, and is composed of 118 hours of speech with its accompanying automatically aligned transcripts.

ted lium an automatic speech recognition.subject: ASR system
ted lium an automatic speech recognition.claim: The authors built an ASR system using the TED-LIUM data leading to a WER score of 17.4 %.
ted lium an automatic speech recognition.quote: We describe the content of the corpus, how the data was collected and processed, how it will be publicly available and how we built an ASR system using this data leading to a WER score of 17.4 %.

ted lium an automatic speech recognition.subject: IWSLT 2011 Evaluation Campaign
ted lium an automatic speech recognition.claim: The official results obtained at the IWSLT 2011 evaluation campaign are discussed in the paper.
ted lium an automatic speech recognition.quote: The official results we obtained at the IWSLT 2011 evaluation campaign are also discussed.

fairness through awareness.subject: framework for fair classification
fairness through awareness.claim: The paper presents a framework for fair classification comprising a task-specific metric for determining individual similarity and an algorithm for maximizing utility subject to the constraint that similar individuals are treated similarly.
fairness through awareness.quote: The main conceptual contribution of this paper is a framework for fair classification comprising (1) a (hypothetical) task-specific metric for determining the degree to which individuals are similar with respect to the classification task at hand; (2) an algorithm for maximizing utility subject to the fairness constraint, that similar individuals are treated similarly.

fairness through awareness.subject: fair affirmative action
fairness through awareness.claim: The paper presents an adaptation of their approach to achieve 'fair affirmative action,' which guarantees statistical parity while treating similar individuals as similarly as possible.
fairness through awareness.quote: We also present an adaptation of our approach to achieve the complementary goal of "fair affirmative action," which guarantees statistical parity (i.e., the demographics of the set of individuals receiving any classification are the same as the demographics of the underlying population), while treating similar individuals as similarly as possible.

fairness through awareness.subject: relationship of fairness to privacy
fairness through awareness.claim: The paper discusses the relationship of fairness to privacy, specifically when fairness implies privacy and how tools from differential privacy may be applied to fairness.
fairness through awareness.quote: Finally, we discuss the relationship of fairness to privacy: when fairness implies privacy, and how tools developed in the context of differential privacy may be applied to fairness.

the security of machine learning.subject: taxonomy of attacks against machine learning systems
the security of machine learning.claim: The paper presents a taxonomy that identifies and analyzes attacks against machine learning systems.
the security of machine learning.quote: We present a taxonomy identifying and analyzing attacks against machine learning systems.

the security of machine learning.subject: taxonomy of attacks against machine learning systems
the security of machine learning.claim: The taxonomy shows how attack classes influence the costs for the attacker and defender and provides a formal structure defining their interaction.
the security of machine learning.quote: We show how these classes influence the costs for the attacker and defender, and we give a formal structure defining their interaction.

the security of machine learning.subject: SpamBayes
the security of machine learning.claim: The taxonomy is illustrated by showing how it can guide attacks against SpamBayes, a popular statistical spam filter.
the security of machine learning.quote: We also illustrate our taxonomy by showing how it can guide attacks against SpamBayes, a popular statistical spam filter.

the security of machine learning.subject: taxonomy of attacks against machine learning systems
the security of machine learning.claim: The taxonomy suggests new lines of defenses.
the security of machine learning.quote: Finally, we discuss how our taxonomy suggests new lines of defenses.

calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.subject: Calibrating Noise to Sensitivity
calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.claim: Privacy can be preserved by calibrating the standard deviation of the noise according to the sensitivity of the function f.
calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.quote: We extend the study to general functions f, proving that privacy can be preserved by calibrating the standard deviation of the noise according to the sensitivity of the function f.

calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.subject: Calibrating Noise to Sensitivity
calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.claim: For several particular applications, substantially less noise is needed than was previously understood to be the case.
calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.quote: The new analysis shows that for several particular applications substantially less noise is needed than was previously understood to be the case.

calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.subject: Indistinguishability of transcripts
calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.claim: The first step is a very clean characterization of privacy in terms of indistinguishability of transcripts.
calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.quote: The first step is a very clean characterization of privacy in terms of indistinguishability of transcripts.

calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.subject: Interactive sanitization mechanisms
calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.claim: Interactive sanitization mechanisms have increased value over non-interactive ones.
calibrating noise to sensitivity in priv.quote: Additionally, we obtain separation results showing the increased value of interactive sanitization mechanisms over non-interactive.

bert pre training of deep bidirectional.subject: BERT
bert pre training of deep bidirectional.claim: BERT is a new language representation model designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.
bert pre training of deep bidirectional.quote: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models (Peters et al., 2018a; Radford et al., 2018), BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

bert pre training of deep bidirectional.subject: BERT
bert pre training of deep bidirectional.claim: The pre-trained BERT model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks without substantial task-specific architecture modifications.
bert pre training of deep bidirectional.quote: As a result, the pre-trained BERT model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks, such as question answering and language inference, without substantial task-specific architecture modifications.

bert pre training of deep bidirectional.subject: BERT
bert pre training of deep bidirectional.claim: BERT obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5, MultiNLI accuracy to 86.7%, SQuAD v1.1 question answering Test F1 to 93.2, and SQuAD v2.0 Test F1 to 83.1.
bert pre training of deep bidirectional.quote: It obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5 (7.7 point absolute improvement), MultiNLI accuracy to 86.7% (4.6% absolute improvement), SQuAD v1.1 question answering Test F1 to 93.2 (1.5 point absolute improvement) and SQuAD v2.0 Test F1 to 83.1 (5.1 point absolute improvement).
